notes.meaning: Jesus traveled into Judea and the area east of the Jordan River. Crowds gathered around Him again, and as He always did, He began teaching them. Even people who have already heard God's truth need to hear it again to keep growing.

Pharisees came to question Jesus about whether a man is allowed to divorce his wife. They were not asking to learn God's will, but were setting a trap to get Him into trouble. They hoped His answer would make Him enemies or contradict Jewish teachers.

Jesus replied by asking what Moses had commanded them in the Scriptures. He pointed them back to the written Word of God rather than human opinions. God's original law is always the right starting place for answering difficult questions.

The Pharisees answered that Moses allowed a husband to write a certificate of divorce and send his wife away. Moses permitted this legal paper to protect the wife from being abandoned without proof that she was free. It was meant to limit rash breakups, not encourage them.

Jesus explained that Moses wrote that rule only because the people had stubborn and hard hearts. It was a temporary concession to human sin, given to prevent worse cruelty. God's true plan for marriage was never meant to include divorce.

Jesus pointed back before the law of Moses to the very beginning of creation. God originally made human beings male and female to complement each other. Marriage between one man and one woman was established by God from the start.

Jesus quoted Genesis to explain that a husband leaves his parents and is joined to his wife. The two are united so closely that God sees them as one single flesh. Because this bond is so deep, marriage is designed to last for a lifetime.

Jesus declared that no human being has the right to tear apart what God has united. God Himself binds a husband and wife together in holy marriage. We must honor the sacred promises made before God and protect our homes.

Later, when they were inside a house, the disciples asked Jesus about this teaching again. Away from the crowd, they wanted Him to explain His strict words about marriage. Jesus used this private moment to make His meaning completely plain to them.

Jesus warned that anyone who divorces a spouse and marries another commits adultery against that spouse. Adultery means being unfaithful to the marriage promise. In God's eyes, the original bond remains binding, and this standard applies equally to husbands and wives.

differ.view: Divorce and remarriage are allowed when a marriage is broken by adultery or when an unbelieving spouse abandons the home.
Divorce and remarriage are never permitted, and any remarriage while an original spouse lives is considered ongoing adultery.

notes.meaning: People brought small children to Jesus so that He would touch them and pray for them. The disciples scolded the parents and tried to stop them from bothering Jesus. They wrongly thought children were not important enough for the Master's time.

Jesus became very upset when He saw His disciples pushing the children away. He ordered them to let the little children come to Him and not stop them. He announced that the kingdom of God belongs to people who have the simple trust of children.

differ.view: Infants can receive faith and belong to God's kingdom, so parents should bring them to Christ in baptism.
Christ welcomes the children of believers into His covenant family, which supports the practice of infant baptism.
This passage encourages bringing young infants to Christ in baptism, and it forms part of the church's baptism service.
Jesus blessed these children with prayer rather than baptizing them, because baptism requires personal faith that infants cannot yet profess.

other.label: Catholic
other.view: This verse gives hope that God provides mercy and salvation for infants who die before they can receive baptism.

notes.meaning: Jesus stated that anyone who does not receive God's kingdom like a little child will never enter it. A child does not try to earn a gift but simply takes it with open hands. In the same way, we must depend entirely on God's grace instead of our own goodness.

Jesus gathered the little children into His arms, laid His hands on their heads, and blessed them. He showed warm and tender love to each child. His gentle welcome proves how deeply God values every young life.

A man ran up eagerly and knelt down before Jesus on the road. He called Jesus a good teacher and asked what he must do to inherit eternal life. He treated eternal life as a reward he could earn through his own good deeds.

Jesus asked the man why he called Him good, reminding him that God alone is truly good. Jesus was not saying that He was sinful, but was urging the man to realize who He truly was. If Jesus is perfectly good, then He is truly God in human flesh.

Jesus reminded the man of the commandments that teach how to treat other people. These include commands not to kill, commit adultery, steal, lie, or cheat, and to honor parents. Loving our neighbors fairly is one clear way we show our love for God.

The man replied that he had kept all these commandments ever since he was a boy. He believed he had lived an upright life on the outside. However, he did not realize that God's law requires perfect love in the secret thoughts of the heart.

Jesus looked at the young man with deep love and told him that he still lacked one thing. He told him to sell his possessions, give the money to the poor, and follow Him. Jesus laid His finger on the man's secret idol, showing him that he loved money more than God.

The man's face fell at these words, and he walked away full of grief. He had vast wealth and was not willing to give it up to follow Christ. His love for money kept him from receiving the eternal treasure Jesus offered.

Jesus looked around at His disciples and remarked how hard it is for wealthy people to enter God's kingdom. Wealth brings many temptations and easily makes people feel self-sufficient. Riches become dangerous when they keep us from leaning completely on God.

The disciples were stunned by His words, since they thought wealth was a sure sign of God's blessing. Jesus spoke tenderly to them as children and repeated His warning. He showed them that trusting in riches creates a terrible barrier to entering God's kingdom.

Jesus used a vivid picture, saying it is easier for a giant camel to go through a sewing needle's tiny eye than for a rich person to enter God's kingdom. He meant that a person cannot save himself while holding on to wealth as an idol. Without God, it is completely impossible.

other.label: Popular modern teaching
other.view: The eye of a needle was a low night gate in Jerusalem where a camel had to be unloaded and crawl through on its knees.

notes.meaning: The disciples were completely astonished and asked one another who could ever be saved. If even the rich and outwardly moral could not get into heaven, salvation seemed impossible for anyone. Their fear showed they were beginning to realize that human effort can never save a soul.
